history.summary: The shrine of Mawli (Maoli) Mata at Sirasar Chowk, Jagdalpur — the pre-Kakatiya presiding deity of Bastar, revered as the elder sister of Goddess Danteshwari, and a synthesis of tribal goddess worship and Hindu Shaktism. She is the central figure of the 75-day Bastar Dussehra: the flower-chariot (phool-rath) circumambulates the Maoli Temple every evening during the festival, the 8-wheeled chariot runs its inner circuit (Bheetar Raini) around it on Vijayadashmi, and during Maoli Parghav she is received here as chief guest, borne in the doli of Danteshwari from Dantewada. The temple's founding history is UNVERIFIED; she predates the Kakatiya-era Danteshwari cult. Coordinates are approximate (Sirasar Chowk area, Jagdalpur; city-centre coordinates used).

town_description: Jagdalpur is the headquarters of Bastar district and the Bastar division in southern Chhattisgarh, once the capital of the princely state of Bastar. Often called the 'Gateway to Bastar' and the tourism capital of Chhattisgarh, it lies amid dense forests, waterfalls (Chitrakote, Teerathgarh) and the tribal heartland of the Gond and Maria communities. It has been the seat of the Bastar royal family since the capital shifted there under Dalpat Deo, and it hosts the world-famous 75-day Bastar Dussehra.
